answer: Each identity runs one saffron lot and locks an 80-credit bond. At harvest it seals a mirror sample in a shale vault and files its dye claim. An auditor re-measures the sample; a claim off by more than 3 points, or a sample reused across lots, burns the bond. The first assay costs 30 credits, the kth 30+6(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 6,024 and 1,000 false lots cost 3,027,000 in fees plus 80,000 locked, no bulk discount. A rented-lot ring fails because the sample carries the lot seal, mismatching the shale vault record. An honest grower pays 30 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
